name: MIRIX

paper.title: MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents

construction.unit: typed entry (e.g. episodic: event_type, summary, details, actor, timestamp)
construction.kept_as: LLM-written summaries/details; Resource and Knowledge Vault keep verbatim content
construction.processing: Meta Memory Manager routes input to per-type Memory Managers, which write in parallel
construction.writer: multi-agent LLMs (gpt-4.1-mini on LoCoMo; Gemini 2.5 Flash on ScreenshotVQA)

organization.stores: Core, Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Resource, Knowledge Vault
organization.index: sqlite; embedding, BM25 and string-match search

management.operations: Memory Managers update own store avoiding redundancy; Core rewritten above 90% capacity

retrieval.candidates: top-10 entries from each of the six stores (active retrieval)
retrieval.selection: Chat Agent picks stores and method (embedding_match, bm25_match, string_match)

use.context: source-tagged retrieved memories injected into the system prompt
use.reasoning: Chat Agent runs targeted tool searches, consolidates, then answers

stages.ingestion: New input (text or screenshots) triggers a search over the memory base; input plus retrieved context go to a Meta Memory Manager.
stages.construction: The Meta Memory Manager routes content to per-type Memory Managers that write structured entries (e.g., episodic: event_type/summary/details/actor/timestamp; semantic: name/summary/details/source) in parallel, avoiding redundancy.
stages.organization: Six typed stores: Core (persona + human blocks), Episodic, Semantic, Procedural, Resource, Knowledge Vault (verbatim sensitive values with access control).
stages.update: Memory Managers update their own stores; Core Memory is rewritten when above 90% capacity; the Chat Agent can directly request precise updates.
stages.retrieval: Active Retrieval: the agent generates a topic from context and retrieves the top-10 entries from each of the six stores into the system prompt; the Chat Agent can additionally call embedding_match, bm25_match or string_match on chosen stores.
stages.answer: Chat Agent consolidates retrieved, source-tagged memories and synthesizes the response.

summary: Multi-agent memory with six typed stores (core, episodic, semantic, procedural, resource, knowledge vault) coordinated by a meta memory manager, with topic-based active retrieval.
notes:
AXES-CHECK: consistent with the paper; retrieval is 'topic search per store' (top-10 per store) plus agent-chosen embedding/BM25/string-match tool calls. Some stores keep verbatim content (Resource Memory, Knowledge Vault), so fidelity tagged mixed. No peer-reviewed venue found (arXiv preprint as of 2026-09). Also evaluated on the multimodal ScreenshotVQA (not recorded as it is not a conversational-memory benchmark).
DESIGN: Sec 3.1-3.3, 4.1.2. Corrected prefill: 'meta-manager routing' kept in construction.processing but made concrete; kept_as changed from 'rewritten' because Resource Memory and Knowledge Vault store verbatim content. conflicts/forgetting null: no contradiction handling or deletion policy described (only Core Memory compaction).

sources.code_note: Branch public_evaluation, which the paper names as its evaluation code (§4.1.2, footnote 3). Commit 7b143c50 (2025-07-12, 'finish public_evaluations') is the first commit on that branch after paper v1 (2025-07-10). Later commits on the branch (to 33e4bde5, 2025-08-20) change the run scripts and a sqlite fix, not the memory or retrieval code read here.

abstract.text: MIRIX splits an agent's long-term memory into six typed stores: core facts about the user and agent, time-stamped episodes, semantic knowledge, procedures, resources such as documents, and a vault for exact sensitive values. A meta memory manager decides which stores new input concerns, and one LLM manager per store writes and edits its entries in parallel. Before answering, the chat agent writes a short topic, retrieves the best matches from each store into its prompt, and can search further with tools. The authors report 85.38 on LoCoMo with gpt-4.1-mini and higher accuracy than retrieval and long-context baselines on ScreenshotVQA, a new benchmark of one to four weeks of screenshots.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

fields.name: human block

units.name: Episodic event
units.role: one time-stamped event, the main store for LoCoMo
units.made_by: Episodic Memory Manager (LLM), one insert, merge or replace call per write

fields.name: summary
fields.what: one-line LLM summary of the event

fields.name: details
fields.what: longer LLM description of the event; prompt asks to record as much as possible
fields.src: code episodic_memory_agent.txt L16; details embedding searched in agent.py L1190; text returned only by search_in_memory (base.py L104-L115)

fields.name: occurred_at
fields.what: event time; the 10 most recent events are always shown

fields.name: tree_path
fields.what: LLM category path such as personal > travel
fields.src: code episodic_memory_agent.txt L18; shown as Path in agent.py L1182

fields.name: event_type, actor
fields.what: category of the event and who produced it
fields.src: paper §3.1; returned only by search_in_memory (base.py L113)

units.name: Semantic item
units.role: knowledge about a person, place or concept

fields.name: name, summary
fields.what: entity name and a one-sentence description

fields.name: details
fields.what: longer LLM description; its embedding is matched against the topic

units.name: Procedural, resource and vault entries
units.role: how-to steps, documents and exact values; little used on LoCoMo text

fields.name: procedure summary, steps
fields.what: goal description and a list of steps

fields.name: resource title, summary
fields.what: name and overview of a shared document or file

fields.name: resource content
fields.what: full or excerpted text; not embedding-searchable, only BM25 or string match via the tool

fields.name: vault caption, secret_value
fields.what: exact values such as addresses or keys; high-sensitivity entries excluded from automatic retrieval. Retrieved each turn but left out of the prompt template

Episodic events keep an LLM summary and longer details, both embedded; only the resource and vault stores keep text verbatim.

text: The chat agent first writes a topic; its embedding pulls the top 10 entries of each store into the system prompt as one-line summaries.
The agent may then call a search tool on a chosen store, field and method, which returns full details, before it answers.

discussion.takeaway: Route memory into typed stores, each kept by its own LLM manager, and put topic-matched summaries from every store into the prompt before answering. With gpt-4.1-mini this reaches 85.38 on LoCoMo, close to full context (87.52).

claims.claim: State of the art on LoCoMo among memory systems.
claims.evidence: 85.38 overall vs Zep 79.09, LangMem 78.05, Mem0 62.47 and RAG-500 51.62, all with gpt-4.1-mini; full context 87.52. Table 2

claims.claim: Largest gains on multi-hop questions, because events are stored already consolidated.
claims.evidence: Multi-hop 83.70 vs full context 77.70 and Zep 69.16. Table 2, §4.3

claims.claim: Much better and far smaller than retrieval and long-context baselines on screenshots.
claims.evidence: ScreenshotVQA accuracy 0.5950 vs SigLIP@50 0.4410 (+35%) and Gemini 0.1166 (+410%); storage 15.89 MB vs 15.07 GB and 236.70 MB. Table 1, §4.2

claims.claim: Runs are stable enough that MIRIX stays best across repeats.
claims.evidence: Three runs 83.98, 87.34, 84.82 overall. Table 3, App. A

limits: Open-domain questions gain least; the authors attribute this to relying on retrieval, which lacks a global view of the conversation.
Some single-hop misses come from ambiguous questions where the stored consolidated event replaces an earlier plan.
Harder real-world benchmarks are left for future work.
reading: There is no ablation: the six-store split, the meta router and topic retrieval are never removed, so the gain over baselines cannot be assigned to any one of them.

In the evaluation code the prompt holds only one-line summaries (10 recent and 10 topic-matched episodes, 10 each from semantic, resource and procedural memory); details reach the answer only through a search tool call. The paper does not report how often the agent calls it.
The knowledge vault is retrieved every turn but the prompt template has no slot for it, so 'top-10 from each of the six components' (§3.2) holds for five stores in the code.
Memory is written one whole LoCoMo session at a time, with instructions to convert relative dates to absolute ones before storing; baselines were run with their own pipelines.
The paper names GPT-4.1 as judge, while the released llm_judge.py at this commit calls gpt-4o-mini with Mem0's prompt.
MIRIX and full context are averaged over 3 runs, the baselines run once; the LangMem gpt-4.1-mini row differs between Table 2 (78.05) and Table 3 (79.22).

The text says MIRIX beats all baselines on multi-hop by over 24 points, but Table 2 shows +14.5 over Zep (69.16) and +6.0 over full context; it also gives 26,000 tokens per LoCoMo conversation (§4.1.1) where the Table 2 caption says 9k.
